name: The Most Holy Name of Mary
ecclesialTitle: Optional Memorial of the Most Holy Name of Mary
briefBio: This memorial honors the personal name Mary, by which Scripture identifies Jesus' mother as a Jewish woman of Nazareth who freely receives God's call. Christian prayer uses her name to remember discipleship and ask intercession, always through Christ and never as a spell, talisman, or guaranteed outcome. The devotion arose locally in early modern Spain and became universal after the 1683 relief of Vienna, joining Marian thanksgiving to a Catholic-Ottoman military conflict. That history must be named without turning Mary into a weapon, degrading Muslims, or sanctifying conquest. The memorial now calls believers to reverent speech, Christ-centered prayer, peace, and the dignity carried by every person's name.

editorial.reviewer: Catholic Daily factual and theological review

whyItMatters: A person's name carries dignity, memory, and relationship. Mary's name can school believers in attentive, Christ-centered prayer and peace when its military reception is faced honestly and never turned against Muslims or any people.
oneMinuteSummary: The Most Holy Name of Mary honors the name by which Scripture identifies Jesus' mother. Luke presents Mary as a Jewish woman of Nazareth who freely receives God's call, visits Elizabeth, and praises God. Her name recalls a person and disciple; it is not a charm, secret formula, or independent source of divine power. The devotion developed locally in Spain and was extended to the universal Roman calendar after the 1683 relief of Vienna from Ottoman forces. That military reception is part of the feast's history, not a mandate for anti-Muslim triumphalism, nationalism, conquest, or civilizational hostility. The Church's modern teaching calls Christians and Muslims to dignity, understanding, and peace. Celebrating Mary's name means following her Christ-centered faith, honoring every person's name, refusing degrading labels, and joining prayer to reconciliation and responsible action. No invocation guarantees victory, healing, protection, or salvation apart from God.

sections.heading: A name in Scripture
sections.body: Luke names Mary within Jewish life at Nazareth and narrates her free response and Magnificat. The memorial begins with a real person and disciple, not an abstract power.

sections.heading: Christ-centered invocation
sections.body: Christian prayer may invoke Mary's name in affection and request for intercession, but salvation belongs to Christ. The name is not a spell, guarantee, substitute for sacraments, or replacement for responsible action.

sections.heading: Spain, Vienna, and military memory
sections.body: The devotion arose locally in Spain and was extended universally after the 1683 relief of Vienna. Its anti-Ottoman setting must be remembered without using Mary against Muslims or baptizing warfare.

sections.heading: A practice of dignity and peace
sections.body: Modern Catholic teaching calls Christians to respect Muslims and work for understanding and peace. Honoring Mary's name should deepen reverent speech and reject slurs, collective blame, and triumphalism.

life.gospelTheme: Mary's name points to a Jewish disciple whose free yes serves Christ and whose praise magnifies God.
life.struggle: A tender devotion became entangled with military victory and can be distorted into magic, nationalism, or hostility toward Muslims.
life.response: Invoke Mary's name through Christ-centered prayer, honor every person's name, face the military history honestly, and practice interreligious respect and peace.

virtues.name: Reverent speech
virtues.evidence: Luke's use of Mary's name holds personal identity, vocation, and praise together.
virtues.imitation: Use a person's chosen name carefully and stop one degrading label or stereotype.

virtues.name: Peacemaking memory
virtues.evidence: The feast's Vienna history and modern Catholic teaching require remembrance without hostility or triumphalism.
virtues.imitation: Learn from a trustworthy Muslim voice and take one local step toward mutual understanding.

practice.spiritual: Pray one Hail Mary slowly, noticing that every phrase leads through Mary's vocation to Jesus and God's grace.
practice.action: Replace one contemptuous label in your speech or community and seek a respectful encounter with a Muslim neighbor or source.

reflectionQuestions: Does my devotional language lead me toward Christ and responsible action, or toward magical expectations?
How can I remember conflict without turning another people into an enemy identity?

scripture.connection: Luke names Mary within a concrete place and vocation, showing that her name recalls a disciple whose freedom and faith serve the coming of Christ.

prayer: God of peace, as we honor the name of Mary, keep our prayer centered on Christ, cleanse our speech of contempt, free devotion from magic and nationalism, and teach Christians and Muslims to meet in dignity, truth, and peace. Amen.
